# 1 Enoch Chapter 101 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Epistle of Enoch

---

**1** Look up at the sky, you children of heaven. Study everything the Most High has made. Fear him. And stop doing evil in his presence.

**2** What will you do if he shuts the windows of heaven and holds back the rain and dew from falling on the earth — because of you?

**3** And if he sends his anger down on you because of what you have done — you won't be able to pray your way out of it. You spoke arrogantly against his righteousness. So you will have no peace.

**4** Watch the sailors on their ships. Don't you see how the waves throw them around, how the winds shake them, how desperate their situation becomes?

**5** They are terrified — because everything they own is on that ship with them. They have this dread in their hearts: the sea is going to swallow us. We are going to die.

**6** But isn't the entire sea — all that water, all its motion — the work of the Most High? Didn't he set boundaries on it and hold it in place with sand?

**7** At his rebuke, the sea shrivels and dries up. Every fish in it dies. Everything in it dies. But you sinners on dry land — you don't fear him at all.

**8** Didn't he make heaven and earth and everything in them? Who gave wisdom and intelligence to everything that moves on land and sea?

**9** Sailors fear the sea. But sinners don't fear the Most High.

---

*PNEUMA notes: The argument is devastating in its simplicity: the sea obeys its Maker without question (v. 7), and sailors are terrified of mere water. But people who have done wrong live without any fear of the God who made the sea. The chapter's rhetorical power comes from this compression in the final verse (v. 9): two facts, side by side, no commentary needed.*
